characterList.description: A blonde woman with shoulder-length, wavy hair. She wears a yellow cardigan and a white shirt. She gestures frequently with her hands while speaking.
characterList.name: Kathy Freston

content_metadata.description: An interview with Kathy Freston discussing her experience watching the film 'Earthlings' and its impact on her life.

qAndA.answer: She uses the terms 'painful' and 'seriously painful,' emphasizing the emotional toll of witnessing the film's content.
qAndA.question: How does Kathy Freston describe her experience watching 'Earthlings'?

qAndA.answer: She argues that while reading or talking about animal cruelty might evoke some reaction, actually seeing the animals' fear and suffering in the film is a profoundly different and more impactful experience.
qAndA.question: What distinction does Kathy make between reading about animal cruelty and seeing it depicted in 'Earthlings'?

qAndA.answer: She calls it a 'killer,' indicating its power to shatter illusions and deeply affect individuals on an emotional level.
qAndA.question: What specific phrase does Kathy use to describe the film 'Earthlings' and its effect on viewers?

qAndA.answer: She realized that consuming animal products contradicted her personal values of kindness and compassion, creating a state of hypocrisy that conflicted with her desired spiritual alignment.
qAndA.question: According to Kathy, how does witnessing animal cruelty relate to the concept of 'spiritual integrity'?

qAndA.answer: She transitioned to a vegan lifestyle, demonstrating a commitment to aligning her actions with her newfound awareness and desire for greater spiritual integrity.
qAndA.question: What action did Kathy take as a result of watching 'Earthlings'?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Oh God, it was painful, seriously painful to watch what happens behind the scenes of
the animal industries.
It's one thing to read about it.
It's one thing to talk about it, but to actually see it, see these animals, see their
eyes, see the fear.
It's a killer, actually.
It's a killer.
That's why I give away the video all the time because you cannot explain to someone what
an animal goes through in the way that Earthlings shows it.
All you have to do is look and you see it's a visceral experience.
It's not pretty.
It's terrible, actually, but it's something that it just rips people over and they go
on the straight way to a more conscious path.
I'm someone who tries to have spiritual integrity in my life and when I started seeing
what happened in animals behind the closed doors, I realized that I wasn't eating with any
integrity at all.
I tried to live by my principles of kindness, compassion and bright living and I realized
what was on my plate had nothing to do with kindness and compassion.
So in a way, I was being a hypocrite and if I wanted to have spiritual integrity, I wanted
to be someone who was conscious and I learned and awake.
I had to see, I had to love, at least if I was keeping eating that way, I had to be aware
and conscious of what was going on.
So when I watched Earthlings, even though I was already on my path, I was awake and aware
and that helped me stick with my institutions.
